ai.title: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.13020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic design automation (EDA) workflows remain highly fragmented, requiring engineers to coordinate heterogeneous representations, specialised software tools, and iterative verification across multiple design stages. Although large language models have brought more general reasoning and code-generation capabilities to EDA, many existing approaches remain focused on isolated tasks and struggle to plan, verify, and repair designs autonomously within executable engineering environments. Here we introduce ChipOmni, a knowledge-enhanced, context-evolving AI agent framework for EDA. ChipOmni integrates multimodal understanding, dynamic planning, multi-agent collaboration, and verification-driven tool interaction into a unified autonomous system. By continually incorporating feedback from external engineering tools, the framework maintains an evolving task context, integrates domain knowledge, and iteratively refines intermediate designs. Across benchmarks for analog circuit, RTL, testbench, and formal-assertion generation, ChipOmni improves multiple task-specific measures over the evaluated baselines and solves all 30 AnalogCoder-Pro tasks. In a long-horizon case study, ChipOmni advances a natural-language RISC-V specification through three design levels to a micro-SoC GDSII layout that passes physical sign-off, without human intervention after initialization. ai.title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.13140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Failure taxonomies for LLM reasoning are increasingly reported as measurements: papers state what fraction of a model's errors fall into named categories, then compare those fractions across models. We show that for one such category the reported fraction is largely a property of the measurement procedure. We defined Compositional Collapse (a model notices a required sub-part of a problem, then drops or misapplies it) and measured it across twelve models and eleven languages on a public multilingual math benchmark (2,316 graded records). First, 50.1% of failures carry evidence for more than one category, so the reported plurality depends on the order in which the classifier tests them: reversing two tests moves it in eleven of twelve models, and across all six orderings Collapse's share spans 26.4% to 76.4%. Second, agreement collapses for the category but not for the task. Native speakers of all eleven languages judged 179 transcripts, agreeing with our inspector at kappa = 0.932 on answer correctness but only kappa = 0.093 on Collapse. A second native speaker per language re-rated 142 items; on 121 determinate pairs the two humans agree with each other at kappa = 0.659, while each agrees with the inspector at kappa <= 0.094. Re-running the same inspector model with the human instructions verbatim raises kappa against Human 2 from 0.147 to 0.636, so the gap is largely attributable to the prompt, not the model. ai.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.13487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. Compared to previous versions, this iteration provides enhanced systematicity, superior quality, and a larger scale, while incorporating multimodal signals and supporting every stage of model development. Experiments demonstrate that WoW significantly improves model performance across diverse benchmarks. To facilitate community research, we further provide an interactive platform for graph-based data selection and retrieval.
ai.summary: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization.

ai.title: LLM Validation Makes Minimal-Pair Benchmarks Easier for Language Models
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.13788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimal-pair benchmarks are only as good as their labels, and LLMs are an obvious substitute for costly human validation. We test it on BLiMP (English) and QFrBLiMP (Quebec French), the two public minimal-pair datasets releasing every forced-choice human judgment. Three LLMs validate by forced choice, by rating, and as a panel, scored against human panels of one, three and five judges in two pre-registered phases. On BLiMP, forced-choice validators agree with held-out human majorities more often than five-judge panels, yet catch far fewer pairs whose label humans reject than one judge does. By point estimate, no validator is worth more than one judge. The errors are not random. On both datasets, across 10 open LMs, human-supported pairs that the pre-registered LLM filter flags are 18.9 points harder than those it accepts, in all 70 LM-validator combinations, and harder than pairs a single human judge flags. Filtering thus removes items on which LMs fail but humans do not, raising accuracy more than random removal. A protocol frozen before any output replicates the gap and the lift on Dutch BLiMP-NL. LLM validation makes minimal-pair benchmarks easier for the models they are meant to test; we release code, validator outputs and item-level scores.
ai.summary: Minimal-pair benchmarks are only as good as their labels, and LLMs are an obvious substitute for costly human validation.

ai.title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level R\'enyi Entropy from Particle Decoding for Adaptive LLM Reasoning
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.13414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantifying uncertainty over an entire LLM completion is critical for selective prediction and adaptive compute. Zero-cost signals such as mean token entropy and log-probability are local to tokens or to one completion, and self-consistency needs many extra completions. We show that Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding for power sampling already estimates the normalizing constant of the power distribution, which gives the sequence-level R'enyi entropy (SRE) of the model's completion distribution at zero marginal cost, with a guarantee at every particle budget. A R'enyi chain rule extends this readout to a family of stepwise entropies of any order. We prove that orders above one are tied to the most likely token of each step, which explains why they track log-probability, while the order-1/2 member accumulates the log of per-step search effort. This member is the best zero-cost selective-prediction signal in 10 of 13 settings. On MATH500 its AUROC is 0.022 to 0.044 above log-probability with all four models and within length quartiles, and the same order is selected when each setting is held out. An 8-particle probe identifies the problems that benefit from more particles, and a two-pass policy matches 64-particle accuracy on MATH500 with 34.2% fewer particles over three seeds.
ai.summary: Quantifying uncertainty over an entire LLM completion is critical for selective prediction and adaptive compute.

ai.title: khammoon: From a Linguistic Guideline to a Thai Morpheme Segmenter
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.13012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thai is written without spaces between words, making segmentation a foundational step in most Thai NLP pipelines. Existing tools primarily reproduce the word-level conventions of corpora such as BEST; however, because the notion of a "word" in Thai lacks a unified linguistic consensus, these conventions struggle with productive compounding, leading to arbitrary boundaries and ambiguity in downstream representations. Instead, we propose operating at the morphological level, focusing on khammoon, the smallest atomic unit that carries meaning. Segmenting at the morphemic level provides an explicit, consistent morphological representation that eliminates compounding ambiguity. Crucially, this representation benefits downstream learning: models trained on morphemes perform on par with or exceed word-level baselines across part-of-speech tagging, named-entity recognition, and sentiment classification, demonstrating that linguistic consistency improves representation quality without downstream performance penalty. To operationalize this representation, we translate linguistic principles into a formal decision guideline with near-perfect human agreement ($\kappa \approx 0.99$), scale annotation with an LLM, and correct systematic errors with human labels. ai.title: Democracy Assistance: State Department Should Improve Congressional Notification of Its Use of Certain Legal Authorities
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Federal law contains certain provisions, known as notwithstanding authorities, that allow agencies to provide funding that would otherwise be restricted. Historically, the annual appropriations act has required agencies to notify Congress if they intend to use a notwithstanding authority to provide assistance in countries where U.S. law prohibits U.S. funding. In fiscal years (FY) 2023 and 2024, the joint explanatory statement (JES) accompanying the act included additional directions for providing such notifications. In July 2025 the Secretary of State announced that USAID had ceased to implement foreign assistance. State assumed certain former USAID functions, including some democracy programs, and will submit congressional notifications related to future democracy assistance. While Congress has not included a JES with directions for providing information on notwithstanding authorities with every appropriations act, it did so in fiscal year 2026 and may continue to do so in the future. GAO’s review of 37 State congressional notifications for FYs 2023 and 2024 funding found that 36 of the notifications do not address one of three criteria, specified in Section 7015(c) of the FYs 2023 and 2024 appropriations acts or in their JESs, for reporting the use of notwithstanding authorities. ai.title: Immigration Detention: Changes In Inspections of ICE Facilities Raise Questions About Oversight
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Department of Homeland Security (DHS) detention facility inspections have changed at the same time that the number of immigration detention facilities and the size of the detained population have increased. From April 2025 to April 2026, following a January 2025 Executive Order, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) added over 40 detention facilities that detain noncitizens for over 72 hours. The average daily population of detained noncitizens grew by over 50 percent, to 61,817 individuals, over the timeframe. From fiscal year 2024 to July 2026, three of the four DHS entities that conducted inspections changed the frequency (decreased or increased) or stopped conducting inspections. Changes to Inspections Conducted by DHS Entities from Fiscal Year (FY) 2024 to July 2026 ICE relies on these inspections to identify deficiencies in its facilities and ensure compliance with its detention standards. However, the frequency of inspections has in some cases decreased, there is an increased reliance on self-inspections, and processes for these inspections have changed. ICE has not used evidence, such as data on deficiencies identified through inspections and performance information such as the extent to which facilities are in compliance with their contracts, to determine the effects of these recent changes on facility conditions. ai.title: Commission preliminarily finds TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed in breach of Digital Services Act for harmful ‘rabbit holes’ effect
ai.source_name: 歐盟執委會 數位政策
ai.via: 歐盟執委會 數位政策
ai.raw_summary: Commission preliminarily finds TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed in breach of Digital Services Act for harmful ‘rabbit holes’ effect Anonymous (not verified) Fri, 11/06/2026 - 12:09 The European Commission has preliminarily found TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) for the so-called ‘rabbit hole effect’ of its recommender system. TikTok's ‘For You' feed shows users a continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image. The more a user interacts with a certain type of content, the more TikTok's ‘For You' feed algorithm recommends similar content. This design can be harmful when such endless and repeated exposure involves, for example, content about sadness, isolation or body image. These ‘rabbit holes' can have a detrimental impact on users' mental health, especially that of vulnerable adults and minors. These preliminary findings focus on both risk assessment and mitigation measures. Read the full details in the press release Find further information about: Supervision of the designated very large online platforms and search engines under DSA Digital Services Act - main aspects of the regulation User rights under the Digital Services Act - an overview Related topics Online platforms and e-commerce DSA - Digital Services Act

trade.title: 經濟部貿易救濟審議會就我對韓國及中國大陸非方向性電磁鋼品反傾銷案與對中國大陸特定鋁箔落日調查案作成產業損害之肯定認定
trade.source_name: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞

trade.raw_summary: 經濟部今（9）日召開貿易救濟審議會，會中就我國對韓國及中國大陸冷軋扁軋非方向性電磁鋼品反傾銷案，以及對中國大陸特定鋁箔課徵反傾銷稅屆滿5年之落日調查案等2案之產業損害調查結果進行審議，前者最後認定國內產業遭受實質損害；後者認定國內產業損害可能因停止課徵反傾銷稅而繼續或再發生。 經濟部表示，就電磁鋼品案調查發現，韓國及中國大陸涉案貨物進口量大幅增加且持續降價，自112年起以低於國產品價格銷售，國內產業為維持競爭力被迫跟進減價，惟因減價幅度不及涉案傾銷貨物而流失客戶，導致生產量、產能利用率、內銷量、市場占有率等經濟指標全面下滑，並自113年起內銷出現虧損且逐步擴大。雖然國內產業114年相關經濟指標一度改善，但115年上半年再度轉弱，顯示涉案傾銷貨物進口已對國內產業造成顯著不利影響。 另針對中國大陸特定鋁箔落日調查案，調查發現，課徵反傾銷稅期間涉案貨物進口量雖有減少，但仍以低價與國產品競爭，使得國內產業營運狀況略有好轉後又再度惡化。復考量中國大陸鋁箔產能過剩且出口能力強勁，加上越來越多國家對其鋁箔採行貿易救濟措施或提高關稅，已嚴重限縮其外銷市場。若我國停止課徵反傾銷稅，涉案貨物可能再度低價大量出口至鄰近且其已建立行銷通路的我國市場。在國內需求尚未好轉、產業體質仍然脆弱的情況下，可能使我國特定鋁箔產業之損害繼續或再發生。 經濟部表示，上述2案產業損害認定結果將通知財政部，並由該部提交關稅稅率審議小組審議是否課徵及繼續課徵反傾銷稅。該2案之產業損害調查報告公開版可於今年12月9日起至貿易署網站（網址：https://www.trade.gov.tw/）「經貿往來」/「我國採行之貿易救濟措施」/「案件調查」項下之「調查報告」下載。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：綜合企劃組邱組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7361

trade.raw_summary: 海關近來接獲進口人詢問國外自備模具之費用是否應計入完稅價格等問題，關務署表示，倘進口人有「無償」或「減價」提供賣方用於生產或銷售該進口貨物之物品或勞務，應主動將其計入完稅價格向海關申報，避免因未申報相關費用而須補稅或送查價，影響通關速度。 關務署說明，依據關稅法第29條規定，進口貨物之完稅價格以交易價格為課徵關稅基礎，為確保完稅價格核估之正確性，若進口貨物之實付或應付價格中，未計入下列由買方無償或減價提供賣方用於生產或銷售該貨物之物品及勞務，應將其合理攤計之金額或減價金額計入完稅價格： 一、組成該進口貨物之原材料、零組件及其類似品。 二、生產該進口貨物所需之工具、鑄模、模型及其類似品。 三、生產該進口貨物所消耗之材料。 四、生產該進口貨物在國外之工程、開發、工藝、設計及其類似勞務。 關務署提醒，倘進口人有此類產銷協助費用，應提供買賣合約書、商業發票、付款證明等必要文件供海關審核，若無客觀及可計量之資料，海關將依關稅法第29條第4項規定無法按交易價格核估其完稅價格，籲請進口人注意，避免海關查核時發現短（漏）報，影響自身權益。 新聞稿聯絡人：賴科長 聯絡電話：（02）25505500分機2703

trade.title: 401(k) Plan Investments: DOL Can Take Steps to Prepare for Expected Private Equity Growth
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found Private equity is one type of investment within a broad, undefined category called alternative assets. It differs from publicly traded equity in who can invest in it, how it is valued, and what disclosures are required, among other things. GAO’s review of selected research papers that analyzed private equity investment fund performance found no consensus on the performance of private equity relative to publicly traded equity, which is an important consideration when making investment decisions. GAO found a range of performance findings among research papers we reviewed, as well as ranges in data analyzed, benchmarks for performance comparisons, and methodologies. For example, one group of papers found that private equity funds outperformed publicly traded equity for the sample of funds they analyzed during the specific time-periods studied. The size of the overperformance varied widely. In one paper the benchmarks did not include a risk premium, the excess return that some experts believe a private equity investment should provide to justify higher investment risks. Another group of papers found that private equity funds underperformed publicly traded equity during the time-period studied, accounting for the underlying risk or fees, which can be higher for private equity than for publicly traded equity products. trade.title: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office: Patent Backlog Reduction Efforts Pose Risks to Examiner Retention and Examination Quality
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found The backlog of unexamined patent applications awaiting an initial decision from the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) rose to about 838,000 applications in January 2025. In September 2025, the USPTO announced a goal to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 applications but did not specify a time frame for reaching it. The backlog was last at that level in 2020. To reduce the backlog, the USPTO is requiring patent examiners to review more applications, has decreased examiner training, and has expanded the use of AI patent search tools. As of August 2026, the USPTO reduced the backlog to about 756,000 applications, but average applicant wait times for a final patentability decision had increased by 11 percent since January 2025. GAO’s analysis found that, even with examiners doing more work, the USPTO is unlikely to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 patent applications before 2031 without lowering examiner attrition (see figure). The examiner attrition rate increased from 2.9 percent in fiscal year 2020 to 7.6 percent in fiscal year 2025. The agency is seeking to hire more examiners, but if high examiner attrition continues, it will affect the USPTO’s ability to reduce the backlog. As of August 2026, the 12-month examiner attrition rate was 7.6 percent.
